teaser.text: DoorDash is a marketplace that helps people discover, buy and receive goods from local businesses. Its business depends on making the same transaction worthwhile for the customer, the merchant and the delivery worker.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for DoorDash?

paragraphs.text: The base case assumes the platform rolls out, but benefits arrive gradually. Acquired scale supports revenue while investment, labor costs and dilution absorb much of the operating improvement. The price reaches $119.53 in October 2027 and $144.65 in October 2029. Its 50% probability reflects positive FY2025 EBIT and sustained marketplace growth, balanced against limited evidence of stable EBIT margins.

blocks.heading: How much cash does DoorDash really make?

paragraphs.text: Cash flow follows payments, while profit follows accounting recognition. In 2025, operations produced $2,431 million of cash while net income was $935 million. After $605 million of capital investment, DoorDash reported $1,826 million of free cash flow.

Stock compensation is an ownership cost even when no cash leaves the bank. Employees received $1,051 million in stock compensation in 2025. Subtracting that from free cash flow produces an analytical “real free cash flow” of $775 million. It is not an official accounting measure, but it shows how much of the cash result remains after recognizing the shares granted to employees.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for DoorDash today?

paragraphs.text: P/E means the share price divided by profit per share. DoorDash’s trailing P/E of 101.8 implies roughly $1.91 of recent earnings per share. Its forward P/E of 41.2 implies about $4.72 of expected earnings, so the shares look cheaper only if that forecast proves true. The comparison also works only if both figures use the same kind of profit, including expenses such as share compensation and acquisition costs.

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast points to losses at both forecast dates; it hinges on integration, local density and spending producing durable operating improvement. Management guides to Marketplace GOV of $33,000–$34,000 million for the quarter ending September 2026. Adjusted EBITDA guidance is $950–$1,100 million. For 2026, stock-based compensation is guided to $1,200–$1,300 million. Depreciation and amortization is guided to $1,100–$1,200 million. Merchant-payment timing is expected to reduce the company’s free cash flow by $700–$800 million.

blocks.heading: Has DoorDash kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Xu’s older award included a clearer hurdle based on sustained stock-price performance. Its first portion vested in 2025 after the relevant 180-day average price exceeded US$187.60. A second portion vested after the average exceeded US$226.80. Those conditions show that an explicit promise was met, even though reported annual pay does not capture the full economic value of older awards becoming earned.

blocks.heading: What have DoorDash's last eight quarters shown?

paragraphs.text: Revenue reached $4,454 million, up from $3,284 million a year earlier. Orders reached 970 million and Marketplace GOV approximately $33.1 billion. Deliveroo, the acquired delivery company, supplied much of the difference between headline and underlying growth: excluding it, revenue grew 24% and GOV 23%. The existing marketplace was therefore still expanding strongly.

Marketplace profitability improved. Gross margin rose from 49.0% to 49.9%. Contribution Profit increased from 4.7% to 5.0% of GOV. Adjusted EBITDA rose from $655 million to $914 million. Yet operating income fell from $163 million to $156 million, while net income fell from $285 million to $200 million. Better order economics were being absorbed elsewhere.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in DoorDash's next results?

paragraphs.text: The November 4 results should test the September-quarter guidance and clarify the fourth-quarter investment burden. The December cash-flow close should show whether underlying cash generation improved after separating merchant-payment timing from operating changes. During the first half of 2027, completion of the shared platform should appear in faster product deployment and better productivity, not another delayed deadline.
